conventions.convention: Units and the entire potential-outcome schedule are fixed; inference averages over the known finite assignment law. Zero-probability assignments remain allowed, and interference is permitted unless separately excluded.
The data space has its full power-set sigma-algebra; every real-valued score on that space is measurable.
The Fisher sharp null fixes each unit's response across every allowed assignment. Scores and two-sided centers are predeclared; the inclusive upper tail includes tied scores.
Tie randomization uses strict-tail mass plus an independent continuous Uniform[0,1] variable times tied mass; validity and uniformity include both endpoints of [0,1].
The weak zero-average-effect null is defined in the binary no-interference submodel on all binary assignments and constrains the average fixed unit effect, rather than every unit effect.

load_bearing.statement: For any real score on a finite weighted probability space, the inclusive upper-tail mass evaluated at a draw is superuniform. Strict-tail mass plus an independent Uniform[0,1] variable times tied mass is exactly uniform.

A known finite assignment law randomizes the assignment while units and a real potential-outcome schedule defined on every allowed assignment remain fixed; observations are the assignment and every unit's realized response.

A schedule satisfies the Fisher sharp null when for each unit i there is a value y_i such that Y_i(z)=y_i for every allowed assignment z. A predeclared real-valued score orders assignments by inclusive upper tails.

For every Fisher-sharp schedule and every u∈[0,1], the actual-weight inclusive assignment-tail p-value has probability at most u of being at most u; independent uniform tie randomization gives probability exactly u. No validity is claimed for the weak null unless it is also Fisher-sharp.

seams_checked.note: The assignment-model definition supplies the contract's observation space, units, quantity status, deterministic observation mechanism, full-measure support, conditioning convention, target, and adequacy classifications. It distinguishes latent responses from law-level identifiability and isolates zero-probability assignments.

RCBD and Latin-square allocations preserve finite assignment-law conventions. Paired-effect consumers explicitly impose no interference; the paired contrast theorem embeds its restricted design into the full binary assignment set using zero weights. The Gaussian F theorem separately assumes its response-error model.

The page explicitly treats the assignment prerequisite as context, separates deterministic sign-matrix identities from response-error variance assumptions, and derives no Gaussian law from randomization.

The prerequisite supplies design-based context only. The page expressly conditions exact normal power calculations on their independent normal sampling model and does not infer that model from assignment randomization.

The potential-outcome, exposure, and two-stage definitions retain fixed schedules and declared assignment probabilities. Partial interference and exposure sufficiency are stated as additional assumptions rather than consequences of randomization.

The Fisher corollary assumes invariance of the full censored record, encodes records injectively as real responses, and extends the predeclared score to the scalar-response data space. It uses actual assignment weights and independent tie randomization, with no claim under equal hazards or a weak null alone.
